anz.name: Australia / New Zealand (FSANZ Food Standards Code)
anz.rules_effective: Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code: Schedule 19 compilation No. 7 in force 1 Sep 2026 (to Amendment 252); Schedule 18 (S18—8 extraction solvents); Schedule 3 (S3—4); Standards 1.4.2 (residues), 1.4.4 + Schedules 23/24 (prohibited/restricted plants). Pesticide MRLs: Standard 1.4.2/Sch 20 applies in Australia only; NZ uses MPI MRL Food Notice.
sources: Schedule 23 Prohibited plants and fungi (as made)
MPI: NZ MRLs for agricultural compounds

il.name: Israel
il.rules_effective: Public Health Protection (Food) Law 2015 as amended by the Food Reform ('what is good for Europe is good for Israel'): EU food regulations adopted by reference ('adopted provisions') from 1 Jan 2025, starting with contaminants and pesticide residues and extended to further EU acts incl. flavourings 1334/2008 (amendments notified to WTO, G/TBT/N/ISR/1400, Aug 2025). Interim period 1 Jan 2025 - 1 Jan 2028 (extendable 2 yrs) during which legacy Israeli standards and the EU route coexist.
il.pending_changes: Israeli adoption of later EU 2023/915 Annex amendments (public consultation Jan-Feb 2025) and of EU 1334/2008 amendments (notified Aug 2025; Israeli effective dates lag EU application, e.g. ~2 months). Legacy Israeli standards fall away after the interim period (1 Jan 2028, extendable).
sources: Goldfarb Gross Seligman: The New Food Reform entering into force in 2025
USDA FAS GAIN IS2025-0018: Israel WTO notifications (MRLs 396/2005, flavourings 1334/2008, additives)
USDA FAS: Israel seeking comments on maximum levels for contaminants (EU 2023/915)
